params.place: Near Xinxiang, Henan province, eastern edge of the Shanxi and Ordos coal basin region, China
observations: TROPOMI 14-day composite (2026-09-22 to 2026-10-06) shows a top hotspot anomaly of +67.6 ppb above background at this location.
EMIT looked 21 times (2023-02-27 to 2026-06-05); NASA outlined 0 plumes here in the formal product.
5 of 8 recent passes read since 2025-01-01 are candidates, peaking at 1,841.6 ppm·m on 2025-05-28.
3 passes were rejected: 1 too weak, 2 within noise.
VIIRS saw no heat source within 1 km over the last 30 nights; flaring was not observed.

explanations.next_check: Repeated candidates on 5 separate dates support recurrence; a ground inspection or aircraft survey would confirm continuous venting.
Persistent multi-date signal without NASA plume outlines; a follow-up EMIT pass or aircraft survey would distinguish a leak from routine venting.
No heat detected by VIIRS and no flare stack mapped; a night-time VIIRS survey or ground visit would confirm or rule this out.
Only a pipeline is mapped within 2 km; no mining or waste facilities in Overture Maps, though mapping gaps in this coal basin are possible.

gaps: NASA's plume product is nearly empty after 2024, so no formal plume outlines exist for the 5 candidate passes.
EMIT only sees the site on its passes; gaps between passes leave emissions unobserved.
Overture Maps and the public registry may have mapping gaps in this coal basin region.
TROPOMI at ~4 km resolution cannot resolve individual sources within the hotspot.
params.next_collection: A targeted EMIT pass or airborne survey over this site to confirm recurrence and estimate flux.
